newsitem.title: USA: U.S. credit card stocks jump after First USA deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. credit card stocks jump after First USA deal.

text.p: Shares of credit card issuers jumped on Monday after Banc One Corp said it would acquire credit card issuer First USA Inc in a $7.3 billion deal.
The deal sparked speculation that other credit card companies could be snatched up as banks try to bolster their credit card divisions, analysts said.
"Given the lemming approach in the banking industry," it is likely that other deals will follow, said one analyst who declined to be named.
"The deal could highlight the possible synergies between credit card companies and major banks," said Leslie Nelkin, an analyst with Furman Selz.
"There's a number of large banks that have had great difficulty expanding their credit card operations," Nelkin said.
Nelkin upgraded both Advanta Corp and Capital One Financial Corp to buy ratings from hold after the Banc One/First USA announcement.
"There's a limited number of credit card companies out there, so they are all probably acquisition targets," said Hambrecht & Quist analyst Dirk Godsey.
The analysts declined to comment on which credit card issuers would be likely targets or on possible buyers.

While many analysts and traders applauded the Banc One deal, one arbitrageur cautioned that other banks may not follow suit. Many banks may be able to build internal credit card division for less money than buying one, the arbitraguer said.
Advanta's class A shares gained 5-1/2 to 48-5/8, Capital One jumped 5 to 38-1/2 and MBNA Corp increased 2-1/2 to 33-5/8.
